svg.title: PflegSolar — architecture, reliability and technology choices
svg.desc: First, see the whole system and its users. A thick zoom arrow opens the PflegSolar box. The next zoom opens only the Python analysis application. Labels and line styles distinguish actions, responses, MQTT messages and zoom connections. Our database and files are inside the logical system boundary, regardless of hosting. A separate reliability panel records the website, backend and database availability targets, outage behaviour, backups and cost trade-offs. Five technology cards describe the tools we reuse and the rules we build. Logging, monitoring and troubleshooting are planned separately; no alert thresholds, log-retention period or monitoring product is chosen.
svg.text: Helps solar panel owners decide whether cleaning is worth the cost, find cleaners and book the job.

g.text: Expected net benefit must be positive
Same data store as in view 2
Repeated here to show its link
About 8 h 46 min downtime in a 365-day year · a design goal, not a customer guarantee
Check the complete dashboard and booking journey. Three component targets alone do not prove this result.
Power generation remains independent of our website.
Show the last reading with its time; mark it out of date.
Reconnect; missing readings are not zero production.
Keep earlier advice visible with its date.
Send no automatic request without enough evidence.
Explain that booking is temporarily unavailable.
Keep backups and practise restoring them.
Show success only after a booking has been saved.
Check who is allowed to accept the offer.
Accept only one cleaner for the same job.
Handle retries without creating a second booking.
What needs protection, and what can wait?
Protect saved bookings and history with backups and tested recovery. Charts and advice can wait briefly.
One application server is a possible simple start; its failure affects every application running on it.
Supabase is a separate dependency. Extra running copies cost more; the hosting setup remains to be agreed.

svg.text: Technology choices · tools we reuse and parts we build

g.text: Alert support when action is needed.
Find the failed step and recover
Find the failed connection or step.
Follow a job using its request ID.
Time in UTC, importance, component and event.
Outcome, reason or error; site/request IDs where relevant.
Keep event-specific details together in a nested JSON object.
Keep private information out of logs
Separate operational events from measurement history
Passwords, tokens, access keys, raw photos and full addresses.
Keep electricity measurements in the measurement store.
Logs record events about those readings, not every raw value.
